Layout

The scaffolding the components sit in: containers that set the measure, a twelve-column grid for page structure, and a small set of flex utilities for everything inside a component.

Masonry

Items of unequal height packed so the short ones leave no gap below them. A grid cannot do this — every cell in a row is as tall as the tallest — so the fallback is CSS columns.

Short

A single line.

Tall

Columns fill one at a time rather than row by row, which is the one thing worth knowing about this layout: the reading order runs down the first column and only then moves to the second.

Medium

Two lines of filler, so the column heights come out uneven.

Short

Another one.

Tall

Each item sets break-inside: avoid, without which a card can be split down the middle and continue in the next column.

Medium

The column count drops to two below 1024px and to one below 720px.
warning
Reading order is not visual order CSS columns fill top-to-bottom, left-to-right, so the item visually second from the top-left is the fourth in the DOM. A screen reader, the Tab key and Ctrl + F all follow the DOM. Where the order carries meaning — a ranked list, a sequence of steps, anything numbered — use .gallery or the grid instead and accept the gaps.

.masonry-fluid sizes by item width rather than a column count, the way an auto-fit grid does. Set --masonry-columns, --masonry-gap or --masonry-min to tune it.

There is a @supports (grid-template-rows: masonry) block ready for the grid-native version. The declaration is invalid where it is unsupported, so the columns above simply stay in force and nothing has to detect anything. Where it does land, grid order is row-major, so the reading-order problem above disappears with it.

Container queries

A media query asks how wide the viewport is, which is the wrong question for a component that can be dropped into a sidebar, a dialog or a full-width band. Mark an element .cq and its children can ask how much room it was given.

Drag the handle at the lower-right. The viewport never changes; only the box does.

Art

A card that reads its own width

Stacked below 420px of its own width, side by side above it, and roomier again past 640px. Put this same card in a sidebar and it stacks; put it in a hero and it spreads — with no change to the markup and no breakpoint to maintain.

Container query units work the same way: .cq-fluid-title is set in cqi, which is a percentage of the container's inline size rather than the viewport's, so the type scales with the component.

Sized in cqi

One catch worth knowing: an element with container-type: inline-size becomes a containment context, which means its children can no longer affect its width. That is exactly what makes the query answerable, and it is also why a container cannot be sized by its own contents.

Spacing utilities

A deliberately short list — top and bottom margins, and padding on all sides. Anything more specific belongs in the component, not in a utility.

Margin

.m-0   margin: 0
.mt-1 … .mt-8   margin-top
.mb-1 … .mb-8   margin-bottom

/* 1:4  2:8  3:12  4:16
   5:24 6:32 8:48 px   */

Padding

.p-0   padding: 0
.p-2 … .p-6   padding, all sides

/* Everything else comes from
   the gap on a .stack or .row */

Breakpoints

Two of them, both max-width, both in one place in the stylesheet. Most responsiveness is handled by the auto-fitting grid instead, which needs none.

BreakpointWidthWhat changes
Large and up1025px +Full twelve-column grid; the table of contents is visible.
Medium≤ 1024pxNarrow columns pair up; wide columns go full width; .hide-lg hides.
Small≤ 720pxEvery column goes full width; sections tighten; .hide-sm hides.

Visibility helpers

Hidden at ≤ 720px Hidden at ≤ 1024px Shown only at ≤ 720px Always visible

Markup for the page shell

<body class="page">
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to content</a>

  <header class="topbar topbar-dynamic">…</header>
  <aside class="drawer" id="site-drawer" data-open="false">
    <nav class="drawer-body" data-site-nav></nav>
  </aside>

  <main id="main" class="page-body">
    <section class="page-hero">
      <div class="container">…</div>
    </section>

    <div class="container section">
      <div class="grid">
        <nav class="col-3 hide-lg">…</nav>
        <div class="col-9">…</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </main>

  <footer class="page-footer">…</footer>
</body>
